- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >2.0), true outcome often lags or overshoots — cap forecast at 1.5–2.0x recent high for next 7 days.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >1.5x in 3–5 days, model is underestimating trend — adjust upward by 10–30% for next 10 days.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., 3–5 days), model is missing mean reversion — add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for next 3 days.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model often misses the shift — adjust forecast upward by 0.2–0.5 in first 2 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >3.0 and true outcome is >5.0, model is overconfident — reduce forecast by 20–40% for next 7 days.
